chapter: Streetcar, Cab revival shows and trips abroad
title: Fletcher Henderson's small band at Cafe Society, 1950
summary: Correcting the Encyclopedia, he says he did not work with Oliver in 1950 but used his small-group music with Henderson at Cafe Society, where Henderson had a stroke and Barefield led the rest of the engagement.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: All right, now, then we come back up to Sy Oliver. It says here in 1950 at the Zanzibar. Is that correct?
No, well, I never worked with Sy again after that. After that first time in the Zanzibar, that is when --
Because 1950 I was down to the Cafe Society with Fletcher Henderson. We had a small band.
And then, you know, in those years,

the 1949, '48-49, I was having the sessions down at the Central Plaza, and I was -- I played with, you know, all the different guys down there. And then in 1950 Fletcher Henderson went into the Cafe Society with a small band but they didn't have any music for a small band, so they used my music, and they had a -- because I had all the small music from years before.

And we went into Cafe Society, and that's when Fletcher had a stroke down there, and then I took the band over for the finish of the engagement. Dick Vance was playing trumpet and me on clarinet and Lucky Thompson on tenor and Fletcher and Jimmy Crawford on drums, and I think it was John Brown on bass, I think it was, because I had been in the Cafe before then. I think it must have been 1946 with Wingy Manone.
